question: How does a partial spot-to-spot mass coupling support later coordinate projection without becoming a hard assignment, confidence map or coordinate transform itself?

visual_design: The source overview groups pairwise partial alignment and downstream stacking. The original four-panel transfer separates input identities, capacity/mass constraints, the cost objective and later projection. A symbolic coupling matrix conveys permitted mass allocation without inventing numerical results. Repeated aliases retain six shared identities; optional histology and z branches are explicitly distinguished.
transferable_rules: Record transported mass, capacity inequalities and total mass separately from confidence or required one-to-one assignment; separate cost mixing alpha from overlap s.
Coupling feasibility does not establish every downstream geometric operation; retain unknown endpoint applicability and separately sourced display-axis assignment.
Check actual editable equation glyphs and rules across final SVG/PDF with pinned fonts; a shared mathematical layout still needs visibility and whole-figure review.
